question: What is the main benefit of taking medication through inhalation regarding how the body processes it?

options.A: It needs liver enzymes to become active
options.B: It slows down absorption through fat tissues
options.C: It breaks down quickly from stomach acids
options.D: It skips the liver's first-pass breakdown completely

explanation: Drugs breathed into the lungs enter the bloodstream directly without passing through the liver first. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h1)

question: Why do inhaled medications start working so quickly?

options.A: Inhaled drugs travel through the skin directly into veins
options.B: The lungs have a huge surface area and a rich blood supply
options.C: Respiratory tissues have no protective barriers
options.D: The heart pumps the drug straight to the brain first

explanation: A large surface area in the air sacs combined with abundant tiny blood vessels allows the drug to pass immediately into circulation. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h1)

question: What size do drug particles need to be to reach the deep parts of the lungs?
explanation: Only very tiny particles stay suspended long enough to travel down into the small air sacs. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h2)

question: Where do drug particles that are too large usually get stuck in the respiratory tract?

options.B: The left side of the heart

explanation: Large particles cannot easily follow the sharp turns in the upper airway, so they deposit in the mouth and throat instead. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h2)

question: Which type of inhaler requires a fast, forceful breath from the patient to work?
explanation: Dry powder inhalers rely entirely on the force of the patient's breath to pull and scatter the medicine powder. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h3)

question: What is the main reason for using a spacer with a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: To reduce how much drug gets stuck in the mouth and throat
options.B: To remove the need for patient coordination
options.C: To speed up the flow of the medication spray
options.D: To turn liquid medicine into a dry powder

explanation: Spacers trap larger droplets so the patient can breathe the smaller, finer particles smoothly into the lungs. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h3)

question: How do inhaled bronchodilators help open up the airways?

options.B: By relaxing the muscles around the airways

explanation: Bronchodilators widen tight airways by relaxing the smooth muscle layer surrounding the breathing tubes. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h4)

question: Why are inhaled steroids prescribed for long-term asthma care?

options.A: To stop a sudden asthma attack immediately
options.B: To reduce ongoing inflammation and airway swelling
options.C: To speed up the heart rate during breathing trouble
options.D: To thin thick mucus plugs in the large airways

explanation: Steroids work as anti-inflammatory agents to prevent frequent asthma flare-ups over time. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h4)

question: Which check is most important before giving a patient an inhaled breathing medication?

options.C: Listening to lung sounds and checking oxygen levels

explanation: Checking the lungs first helps show if the treatment is really needed and helps measure how well it worked afterward. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h5)

question: Why does a nurse need to check a patient's hand strength and coordination before picking an inhaler type?

options.A: Arthritis stops patients from swallowing pills
options.B: Shaking hands make the medicine expire sooner
options.C: Weak hands cannot hold a nebulizer mask
options.D: Pressurized inhalers require precise timing between pressing and breathing

explanation: Metered-dose inhalers require good hand-breath coordination to press the canister and breathe in at the exact same time. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h5)

question: How long should a patient try to hold their breath after using a metered-dose inhaler?
explanation: Holding your breath for about ten seconds gives the tiny drug particles time to settle deep into the small airways. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h6)

question: Why must patients rinse their mouths out after using an inhaled steroid?

options.A: To clean powder off the front teeth
options.B: To prevent fungal infections like oral thrush
options.D: To wash away a bad taste

explanation: Rinsing washes away any leftover steroid medicine left behind in the mouth, which prevents fungal overgrowth. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h6)

question: What is a common side effect of using rescue inhalers (beta-agonists) frequently?
explanation: Beta-2 drugs can stimulate heart and muscle receptors, leading to an increased heart rate and jittery feeling. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h7)

question: What is the main danger if a home nebulizer machine is not cleaned properly?

options.B: The liquid medicine will dry up too fast
options.D: Bacteria can grow and get breathed into the lungs

explanation: Moist chambers in nebulizers easily collect germs, which can cause lung infections if breathed in. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T19#GNS125_U3_T19_h7)
